newsitem.title: USA: IMF's Camdessus confident of Japanese recovery.
newsitem.headline: IMF's Camdessus confident of Japanese recovery.

text.p: Japan's economy should resume a recovery in the second half of 1997 after stalling as a result of tax changes in the second quarter, International Monetary Fund Managing Director Michel Camdessus said on Tuesday.
Camdessus also said he believed the current rate of the yen was "where it should be" to allow for internal demand-led growth in Japan.

Speaking to reporters, Camdessus said: "I am confident that the economic recovery which has started materializing in the first quarter and which will stop in the second quarter...should start again in the second half of the year.

Camdessus attributed the second quarter pause to changes in Japan's tax structure. Japan's sales tax increased from April 1, with first quarter growth bolstered by a rush in consumer spending ahead of the increase.
He stressed the importance of maintaining and expanding domestic demand in order to establish sustainable growth in Japan, and noted that current currency conditions would help accomplish that.
"I believe the conditions are there and that the yen is where it should be to allow for this type of internal demand-led growth," he said.
